minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District Commissioners heard a resident's appeal over a nearly $5,000 bill caused by a hose left running for months, and agreed informally to flatten billing tiers and arrange a payment plan without finance charges. They also reviewed a draft public survey on future water-treatment options (including PFAS and hardness issues), took detailed public feedback from a resident offering to help refine it, and declined to add an unstudied treatment scenario to the survey. No formal roll-call votes were recorded beyond routine motions.

what_happened.line: Commissioners informally agreed to flatten billing tiers and waive finance charges on a resident's bill run up by a hose left running for months.
Staff will recalculate the adjusted balance and call the resident to set up a monthly payment plan.
The board reviewed a draft public survey on future water-treatment options, including PFAS and hardness, and took detailed resident feedback on its wording.
The board decided not to add an unstudied treatment scenario to the survey, favoring a general question about interest in further options instead.
No formal roll-call votes were taken beyond routine motions; the billing relief and survey changes were reached by informal agreement.

why_it_matters: A leak-driven high bill was resolved case by case rather than through a written policy, which matters for any resident who later disputes a similar bill.
The treatment survey will help shape how the district weighs future PFAS and water-quality investments, which can affect water rates down the line.
Because the commitments were informal rather than voted on, none of tonight's arrangements are yet binding decisions of record.
